summary: Check the Swag Labs login form's mandatory-field error and the site footer: open the inventory URL (which bounces an anonymous visitor to the login page), submit the login form with both fields left empty and validate the resulting error message "Epic sadface: Username is required", then log in as standard_user / secret_sauce, scroll the inventory page to its bottom and validate that the footer message contains the copyright year and the text "Terms of Service". The year the footer shows is the current calendar year, computed by the site from the clock, so the step's literal 2023 is amended to a year derived at run time (deviation D-2.6).
preconditions: Case 0 is merged: the project runs on @playwright/test 1.39.0 with a single browser project, Firefox, and a base address already pointing at the Swag Labs host; the suite runs via `npm test` locally and in CI.
The Swag Labs demo site is reachable and publishes the credentials this case uses on its own login page (accepted usernames include standard_user, password for all users secret_sauce).
Each test run starts from a fresh browser profile, so the first navigation is made by an anonymous visitor and the login form starts empty.
At the project browser's default window size (1280x720) the footer sits below the fold on the page reached after login, so step 2.5's scrolling is really needed to bring it into view.

steps.refined: The test's entry point is the inventory page address named in the step. Opened by an anonymous visitor, the site answers it by sending the browser to the login page, which already shows the alert "Epic sadface: You can only access '/inventory.html' when you are logged in."; the test continues from that login form.

Without typing anything, the test clicks the login form's Login button while both the username and the password field are still empty, which is what makes the site complain about the mandatory fields.

The test asserts that the login form's error message produced by the empty submit is visible and that its text is exactly what the site writes for the first missing mandatory field: "Epic sadface: Username is required" (replacing the access-denied alert that the redirect of step 2.1 had put there).

steps.original: Login with the following credentials: standard_user / secret_sauce
steps.refined: On the same login form the test types the username standard_user and the password secret_sauce, clicks the Login button, and ends up on the inventory page with its product listing shown. The error message left over from step 2.2 does not have to be dismissed first.

steps.original: Scroll down to the bottom of the page
steps.refined: On the page reached in step 2.4 the test scrolls down to the very bottom, so that the footer at the end of the page is inside the viewport.

steps.original: Validate the footer message contains 2023 and Terms of Service
steps.refined: The test asserts that the footer's copyright message contains the copyright year and the text "Terms of Service". The year is not a fixed string on the site: the footer renders the current calendar year from the clock, so the expected year is derived at run time instead of the step's literal 2023 (see deviation D-2.6). Observed today the message reads "(c) 2026 Sauce Labs. All Rights Reserved. Terms of Service | Privacy Policy".

acceptance_criteria.text: The first page the test opens is the inventory page address named in step 2.1, and the test proceeds on the login form the site shows an anonymous visitor there.
The test clicks the login button with the username and password fields left empty, before entering any credentials.
The test asserts that the error message shown after that click is visible and that its text is "Epic sadface: Username is required".
The test logs in through the same form with the username standard_user and the password secret_sauce and reaches the inventory page with its product listing.
The test scrolls the page reached after login down to its bottom, bringing the footer into the viewport, before checking the footer.
The test asserts that the footer message contains the copyright year, with the expected year derived at run time (the current calendar year) rather than hard-coded; see deviation D-2.6.
The test asserts that the footer message contains the text "Terms of Service".

observations: 2026-11-26: opening the inventory page address as an anonymous visitor does not render the inventory; the browser ends on the site root (the login page) and the form shows the alert "Epic sadface: You can only access '/inventory.html' when you are logged in." with a "Dismiss error" button. No HTTP error, no interstitial.

Clicking the Login button with both fields empty replaces that alert with "Epic sadface: Username is required" (exact text, no trailing punctuation) and marks both input fields with an error style. The page does not navigate; the error element is the form's alert region (a heading with role=alert carrying a "Dismiss error" button).
Filling only the username and clicking Login again yields "Epic sadface: Password is required". That second message therefore needs a second submit, which the steps of this case do not ask for.

The login form fields are accessibly named "Username" and "Password" (placeholders), the submit control is a button named "Login"; neither input carries the HTML required attribute, so the error is produced by the site's own validation, not by the browser.

Logging in as standard_user / secret_sauce from that error state works without dismissing the error first and lands on the inventory page immediately (well under a second, unlike performance_glitch_user in Case 1).

On the inventory page at the project browser's default window size (1280x720) the document is 1110 px tall: the footer starts 970 px below the top of the viewport, i.e. it is below the fold and not in view until the page is scrolled. Scrolling to the bottom moves the footer fully into view (its bottom edge coincides with the viewport bottom) and the page's maximum scroll offset is 390 px.

The footer's copyright message, one text line with data-test "footer-copy", reads exactly: "(c) 2026 Sauce Labs. All Rights Reserved. Terms of Service | Privacy Policy" (with the real copyright sign). "Terms of Service" appears in it as plain text, not as a link; the footer's only links are X, Facebook and LinkedIn.

The year in that message is computed, not written: the site's single script bundle renders the line as `["(c) ", new Date().getFullYear(), " Sauce Labs. All Rights Reserved. Terms of Service | Privacy Policy"]`, and the literal "2023" occurs zero times in that bundle (evidence: docs/evidence/case-2/footer-year.md, docs/evidence/case-2/footer-year.png).

No cookie or consent banner, no iframe and no third-party overlay appeared anywhere in the flow. The only console output is one repeated harmless error per page load ("Permissions policy violation: unload is not allowed in this document").

ambiguities.question: Step 2.3 says "validate the error message", but at that moment two different messages have been in the alert: the access-denied alert that the step-2.1 redirect left there, and the one the empty submit of step 2.2 produces. Which one is validated?
ambiguities.decision: The one step 2.2 produces, "Epic sadface: Username is required": the case is titled "Verify error messages for mandatory fields" and step 2.3 directly follows the empty-form click. Asserting that exact text also distinguishes it from the access-denied alert, so a test that never really submitted the empty form would fail.

ambiguities.question: The case title says "error messages" (plural) for mandatory fields - should the password error be validated too?
ambiguities.decision: No. The steps describe one click on the login button and one validation, and the site only reveals "Epic sadface: Password is required" after a second submit with the username already filled. Adding that would be inventing a step; the username error is the message the described interaction produces.

ambiguities.question: Step 2.4 says "Login with the following credentials" without naming the fields or the button.
ambiguities.decision: Do what logging in means on this form: type standard_user into the username field, secret_sauce into the password field, click Login, and wait for the inventory page. The leftover error banner needs no dismissing (verified today).

ambiguities.question: Case 1 reads its credentials from test/resources/credential.json. Should Case 2 read standard_user from a file too?
ambiguities.decision: No. Step 2.4 names its credentials inline and only Case 1 requires a credential file (its steps 1.2-1.3); the credential file holds performance_glitch_user. This case's credentials come from this spec's test data.

ambiguities.question: Step 2.5 says "the page" - which page is scrolled, and does scrolling need its own assertion?
ambiguities.decision: The page reached in step 2.4, the inventory page (steps are sequential). Scrolling is an action, not a validation, so it is satisfied by actually scrolling to the bottom; the footer check of 2.6 is what the scroll serves. The footer is genuinely below the fold at the project's window size, so the scroll is not decorative.

ambiguities.question: Step 2.6 says "the footer message" - the whole footer or the copyright line?
ambiguities.decision: The copyright message line, which is the footer's own message and contains both things the step names (the year and "Terms of Service"); the rest of the footer is only the three social links.

ambiguities.question: The footer cannot contain 2023 any more (it renders the current year). Fail the test, or amend the expected year?
ambiguities.decision: Amend it to the current year derived at run time (deviation D-2.6). The requirement was written while the site showed 2023 and its intent is that the footer carries the copyright year next to "Terms of Service"; a 2026 copyright line in 2026 is correct site behaviour, not a defect to be reported, and hard-coding today's 2026 would rot exactly like 2023 did. Deriving the year from the same source as the site (the clock) keeps the check meaningful; the only theoretical flake is a run crossing midnight on 31 December.

deviations.original: Validate the footer message contains 2023 and Terms of Service
deviations.amended: Validate the footer message contains the copyright year of the current calendar year, derived at run time, and Terms of Service.
deviations.why_unfulfillable: Observed 2026-11-26: the footer message on the page reads "(c) 2026 Sauce Labs. All Rights Reserved. Terms of Service | Privacy Policy". The year is not content but computed - the site's only script bundle renders the line as ["(c) ", new Date().getFullYear(), " Sauce Labs. All Rights Reserved. Terms of Service | Privacy Policy"] - and the literal "2023" occurs zero times in that bundle. The footer showed 2023 only during the calendar year 2023 and can never show it again, so no test can observe it.
deviations.why_this_amendment: Only the year part of the step changes, and it changes to a value derived at run time rather than to today's hard-coded 2026, which would rot in the same way 2023 did. The "Terms of Service" half of the check stays exactly as written, and the check keeps its original strength: the footer must still carry the copyright year, taken from the same source the site uses.

test_data.entry_page: the inventory page address given in step 2.1 (https://www.saucedemo.com/inventory.html)
test_data.empty_submit: login button clicked with both fields empty (no credentials typed)
test_data.footer_page: the inventory page reached after the login of step 2.4
test_data.expected_footer_year: the current calendar year, derived at run time (observed 2026 on 2026-11-26; the step's literal 2023 is amended, see deviation D-2.6)
test_data.observed_footer_message: (c) 2026 Sauce Labs. All Rights Reserved. Terms of Service | Privacy Policy
test_data.browser_project: firefox (the project browser chosen in Case 0)
test_data.observed_viewport_and_scroll: 1280x720 window, document 1110 px tall, footer starts 970 px down, maximum scroll offset 390 px
